description.narrative: The objective of the Human Capital Development Project for Burundi is to empower boys and girls through improved access to quality nutrition, healthcare, and basic education services in Burundi. There are four components to the project, the first component being addressing demand-side determinants for education and health access across the lifecycle. This component includes two subcomponents: scale up demand-side-PBF coverage of key nutrition, and birth control services, and ensuring the most vulnerable learners are ready and equipped to learn. The second component is the improving the supply of education and health services across the lifecycle. This component includes three subcomponents: Improving learning environments, improving teaching, and learning at scale, and capitalizing on the supply-side performance-based financing for healthcare quality. The third component is the improving system governance and project management. This component includes two subcomponents: improving system governance, and project management, monitoring and evaluation. finally, the fourth component is the contingent emergency response.
To increase access to quality health and education services, especially for early childhood.
